newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam records January trade deficit of $367 mln.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam records January trade deficit of $367 mln.

text.p: Vietnam recorded a trade deficit of $367 million in January, an official at the Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
He said exports reached $583 million and imports $950 million. Previous estimates by the General Statistics Office had put the January trade gap at $420 million.
Local newspapers reported on Tuesday that exports climbed by 22.5 percent in January against the same month last year, with leading growth in earnings from coffee, crude oil and textiles.

The Trade Ministry official, speaking by phone, was unable to provide a breakdown or comparitive figures for January last year, but said Hanoi was hoping for year-end exports in 1997 worth $8.5 billion and imports of $11-12.5 billion.

In 1996 the trade deficit reached a record level of $4.0 billion. The issue caused concern for government, prompting calls in some quarters to promote local products over imports and stirring debate over the merits of free trade.
